question: cord route from the spinning pull rings to a travelling root

options.name: Two traveller hoops under the disc rim (keeps K1 and K2+K3 separate)
options.how: Each pull ring carries a steel wire hoop on top; each finger's cord ends in a C-clip bead that slides round its hoop. The cord goes out under the disc rim and up into the finger root.
options.clr: outer bead to the static yoke lip: 0.1 mm; inner cord over the outer bead about 0.6 mm (est.)
options.load: bead 0.3 g at r 26: 13 N outward, held by the hoop
options.parts: 2 x 0.8 mm music-wire hoops, 8 brass C-clips (est.)
options.risk: tightest; two hoops share 4 mm under the disc

options.name: One ring, one hoop: K1 to K3 curl together
options.how: As A with only the outer (base) ring. The inner ring and its servo go; each finger curls all three knuckles from one cord (today's K2+K3 cord path).
options.clr: yoke lip inner edge moved out 0.6 mm (r 27.1 -> 27.7, still 2.3 mm over the flange): bead clears it by 0.7 mm; 3.2 mm of height for one hoop (est. 2.0 used)
options.load: same bead: 13 N on the hoop
options.grip: one curl motion per finger; no separate K1
options.risk: less grip shaping; finger force sharing must be re-sized

options.name: Hanger arm from each root block down past the rim, slotted guide on the ring
options.how: A thin arm hangs from the block outside the disc rim and drags a slider on a rail on the pull ring; the cord runs inside the arm.
options.clr: arm at r 25.7 to 26.9: 0.2 mm to the yoke lip, hits the base ring top when pulled 13 mm down
options.load: arm 0.6 g at r 26 (est.): 26 N bending it outward
options.risk: arm must reach 13 mm down through the moving ring: collides

options.name: Bowden cables with a slack loop round the hub
options.how: Sheathed cable from a fixed anchor on the ring to the root block; the sheath lies in a channel and takes up the root's travel.
options.clr: needs about 80 mm of loose sheath per finger (half a turn at r 25) in a channel outside the rim: no room under the cage
options.load: 80 mm of sheath (est. 1.5 g) at r 28: 72 N of fling
options.risk: friction round half a turn (est. 30 to 50 % loss); fling

options.name: Ball-end cords that drop into 12 cradles on the ring
options.how: Each cord ends in a ball sitting in one of 12 open cradles (every 30 deg). When the root moves, the ball slides out over a ramp and drops into the next.
options.clr: like A (one ring) but the ball must climb out sideways when slack: cradle walls 1.5 mm
options.load: ball 0.5 g at r 26: 22 N, seated by the spin
options.risk: ball can hop to the wrong cradle; needs slack at each move

options.name: Keep everything on the rotor top: pull plate above the hub
options.how: Rings move above the top disc; pulled through a hollow motor shaft by a static rod.
options.clr: SE 2816 shaft is solid dia 5: no rod through it
